entries.test: The Davos January 2026 and Stanford late-May/early-June 2026 transcripts or videos of Hassabis's AGI timeline remarks.
entries.note: At Stanford Hassabis hedged his estimate ('maybe like 2030 plus or minus a year'). 'Around 2030' captures that hedge well enough.

entries.test: Whether AGI meeting Hassabis's all-cognitive-capabilities definition arrives no earlier than 2031 (and, if read literally, by 2036).
entries.note: Marcus backs the more conservative view mainly to argue against AGI this decade. Reading this as a positive commitment to AGI by 2036 goes further than his words, and the 'will_not' modality is muddled.

entries.test: Whether any system meeting Hassabis's definition of AGI (all human cognitive capabilities, including breakthrough creativity and physical intelligence) exists by the end of 2029.
entries.note: 'This decade' is read as ending in 2029. Some readers count the decade through 2030.

entries.test: Whether AI systems as of mid-2026 showed breakthrough scientific or artistic invention and human-level physical and robotic skill.
entries.note: 'Not even close' is vague, but the definition he adopts gives it a plain reading.
